#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script converted from Slurm
# Note: Flux does not support in-script directives for resource specification
# This script should be submitted with the following command:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 4 -c 1 -t 10m --job-name=petscDMDA --output=petscDMDA-{{id}}.out --error=petscDMDA-{{id}}.out script.sh
#
# Resource specifications:
# -N 1         : 1 node (from --nodes=1)
# -n 4         : 4 tasks (from --ntasks=4)
# -c 1         : 1 core per task (from --hint=nomultithread, no hyperthreading)
# -t 10m       : 10 minute walltime (from --time=00:10:00)
# --job-name=petscDMDA : job name (from --job-name=petscDMDA)
# --output=petscDMDA-{{id}}.out : output file with job ID (from --output=petscDMDA%j.out)
# --error=petscDMDA-{{id}}.out : error file with job ID (from --error=petscDMDA%j.out)
#
# Note: Flux uses {{id}} for job ID instead of %j
# Note: Both stdout and stderr redirect to the same file as in original

# Original job name: petscDMDA
# Set at submission: flux batch --job-name=petscDMDA ...

# Original output/error files: petscDMDA%j.out
# Flux equivalent: petscDMDA-{{id}}.out
# Set at submission with job ID placeholder

# Thread affinity hint: nomultithread
# Original: --hint=nomultithread (1 MPI process per physical core, no hyperthreading)
# Note: Flux handles thread/core binding differently
# Using -c 1 (1 core per task) approximates this behavior
# For explicit control over thread affinity, use Flux's cpu-affinity options:
# --setattr=system.shell.options.cpu-affinity=per-task
# Performance impact: Without explicit affinity control, processes may migrate
# between cores or use hyperthreads, potentially reducing performance
# Consult Flux documentation for hwloc-based binding options

# Tasks: 4 MPI processes
# Note: Flux uses -n for task count
# MPI execution will use flux run instead of srun

# Working directory
# Slurm: $SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR provides submission directory
# Flux: $FLUX_JOB_SUBMITDIR provides submission directory
# Or use --cwd flag at submission time
cd ${FLUX_JOB_SUBMITDIR:-$PWD}

# Clean module environment inherited from interactive session
module purge

# Load required modules
source ../../../petsc.sh

# Echo commands being executed
set -x

# Execute the code
# Slurm: srun launches MPI tasks
# Flux: flux run launches MPI tasks within the allocation
# With flux batch, we're already in an allocation, so use flux run
time flux run -n 4 ./dmda.exe -da_grid_x 1000 -da_grid_y 1000 -ksp_type cg -pc_type hypre

# Alternative if direct execution is preferred (requires proper MPI configuration):
# time mpirun -n 4 ./dmda.exe -da_grid_x 1000 -da_grid_y 1000 -ksp_type cg -pc_type hypre

# Note on MPI launcher:
# flux run is the recommended approach for launching MPI tasks within Flux
# It ensures proper integration with Flux resource management and job control
# The -n 4 specifies 4 MPI tasks, matching the allocation

issues: The script correctly documents resource specifications and the conversion from Slurm to Flux is accurate.

The output/error file placeholder uses '{{id}}' which should be verified. Flux typically uses '{{id}}' or '{{jobid}}' for job ID substitution in output filenames. Some Flux versions may require different syntax like '{id}' (single braces). This should be tested with the specific Flux installation.
The submission command documentation is comprehensive and correctly translates Slurm directives to Flux command-line options.
The resource allocation (-N 1 -n 4 -c 1) correctly specifies 1 node, 4 tasks, and 1 core per task, totaling 4 cores on 1 node, which matches the original Slurm specification.

The thread affinity consideration is well-documented. The script notes that Slurm's --hint=nomultithread is approximated with -c 1, but acknowledges that explicit cpu-affinity options may be needed for optimal performance. This is a valid approach.
The script uses 'flux run -n 4' to launch the MPI job, which is correct. The -n 4 matches the allocation specified at submission time.
The working directory handling uses '${FLUX_JOB_SUBMITDIR:-$PWD}' which is a good defensive pattern, falling back to $PWD if FLUX_JOB_SUBMITDIR is not set.
The time limit '-t 10m' correctly converts from Slurm's 00:10:00 format to Flux's simplified format.

No memory limit is specified in either the original Slurm script or the converted Flux version. For PETSc DMDA applications with 1000x1000 grids, memory requirements should be considered. The default memory allocation may be insufficient.

The script sources '../../../petsc.sh' which is a relative path. This assumes the script is run from a specific directory structure. If the submission directory is different from expected, this will fail. Consider using absolute paths or verifying the path exists.
No error checking after 'cd ${FLUX_JOB_SUBMITDIR:-$PWD}'. If the directory change fails, the subsequent commands may execute in an unintended location.
The 'module purge' and 'source ../../../petsc.sh' commands assume a module system is available and configured. There's no error handling if these fail.
The executable './dmda.exe' uses a relative path. If the working directory is not correct, this will fail. Consider verifying the executable exists before running.

#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=petscDMDA       # nom du job
#SBATCH --nodes=1                  # Nombre de noeud
#SBATCH --ntasks=4                 # Nombre total de processus MPI
#SBATCH --hint=nomultithread       # 1 processus MPI par coeur physique (pas d'hyperthreading)
#SBATCH --time=00:10:00            # Temps d’exécution maximum demande (HH:MM:SS)
#SBATCH --output=petscDMDA%j.out   # Nom du fichier de sortie
#SBATCH --error=petscDMDA%j.out    # Nom du fichier d'erreur (ici commun avec la sortie)

# on se place dans le répertoire de soumission
cd ${SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR}

# nettoyage des modules charges en interactif et herites par defaut
module purge

# chargement des modules
source ../../../petsc.sh

# echo des commandes lancées
set -x

# exécution du code
time srun ./dmda.exe -da_grid_x 1000 -da_grid_y 1000 -ksp_type cg -pc_type hypre
